structure.title: Agamemnon · The signal fires
structure.text: A watchman sees the sign that Troy has fallen. The army's victory brings a husband back to a house with an outstanding claim against him. His captive Cassandra sees things in that house which the citizens standing beside her cannot bear to understand.

structure.title: The Libation Bearers · An offering at a grave
structure.text: Orestes returns to his father's grave and finds his sister there. A command to avenge a parent has an impossible feature in this particular family. To fulfil his duty to one parent he must commit a crime against the other.

structure.title: The Eumenides · A city agrees to hear the case
structure.text: The pursuit travels from Delphi to Athens. A rule is needed for deciding which claim takes precedence and who may announce the decision. Establishing a court still leaves the question of what the losing side could gain by accepting it.

people.name: Clytemnestra
people.role: Queen ruling in her husband's absence
people.text: She remembers the daughter sacrificed before the fleet sailed. The army's return home means something different to the woman who stayed behind and kept count of the cost.

people.name: Orestes and Electra
people.role: Children surviving a quarrel between parents
people.text: The pair discover what they can share as mourners. A god's instruction and their father's grave lend authority to an act whose consequences Orestes must face in his own person.

people.name: The Furies
people.text: The audience eventually sees the figures Orestes fears. They have arguments, interests and a conception of justice. A court that orders them to stop must reckon with the injuries they exist to avenge.

context.title: Iphigenia and the fleet
context.text: Agamemnon sacrificed his daughter so the fleet could sail for Troy. The expedition celebrated as a public victory began with a killing for which nobody has offered her mother satisfaction.

notice.text: Hear each new chorus claim the stage.
notice.why: Elders at Argos, women bearing offerings and ancient goddesses have different access to power. A voice once limited to commentary can become a party to the case.

notice.text: Follow the chain of acts called due payment.
notice.why: A deed somebody calls repayment can generate another debt for the next generation. The difficulty for Athens is to bring this accounting to an end in a way that can hold.

opening: The war is over, and Agamemnon is coming home to a wife who remembers what he sacrificed to get his ships to Troy. Victory has not settled the debt inside the family. Aeschylus follows a succession of people who can justify their next act of violence by pointing to the last one. Across three plays, the need to punish becomes a problem that revenge cannot finish solving, and the possibility of judgment by a community has to contend with grievances that will not quietly disappear.
